scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The official increase notice and any accompanying landlord explanation are needed to verify the prescribed form, stated effective date, reasons, and calculation.
The prior rent statement is needed to establish the previous rent and reference-rate basis for checking the increase calculation.
The envelope and, if the notice was sent registered, the delivery receipt are needed to establish the notice's dispatch and receipt dates for the challenge deadline.
The applicable official reference-rate publication is needed to verify whether the asserted rate adjustment is mathematically justified.
The official rent-increase form is needed to verify the prescribed form, stated reasons, old and new rent, effective date, and challenge information.
Available delivery evidence is needed to establish the date of receipt and calculate the 30-day challenge deadline.
The prior rent statement and applicable reference-rate publication are needed to identify the previous calculation basis and check the asserted increase.

These records are needed together to compare the rent amounts charged with the amounts actually paid under the standing orders.
The prior and current increase notices and related management communications are needed to establish the stated reference-rate grounds, notification dates, and effective dates.
The rent ledger and a management statement are needed to reconcile the applicable net-rent baseline with each rent debit and determine whether the earlier increase was actually posted.
Payment records and bank statements are needed together to compare the rent amounts demanded with the amounts actually paid under the standing orders.
The applicable official reference-rate publication is needed to verify whether both notices rely on the same rate change.

Obtain the current and prior autumn rent-increase notices and related landlord communications to establish their stated effective dates, reference-rate grounds, and the alleged system error.
Obtain the management ledger and prior rent statements to reconcile the contractual net-rent baseline with each rent debit actually posted.
Obtain the rent-payment records and corresponding bank statements to compare the amounts demanded with the amounts actually paid over the relevant periods.

requests.why: These documents are needed to verify the mandatory form, stated old and new rent/ancillary-cost amounts and reasons, and the date of receipt for the 30-day challenge deadline.
These are needed to establish the previously applicable net rent and ancillary-cost advance separately from the new allocation.
A numerical breakdown of the asserted cost adjustment is needed to assess whether the increase in net rent and reduction of the heating-cost advance are substantiated.
The official notice and its envelope are needed to verify the stated old and new net/ancillary amounts, the grounds given, and the date of receipt for the challenge deadline.
The prior rent statement is needed to establish the binding previous net rent and ancillary-cost advance against which the new amounts must be compared.
These documents are needed together to obtain a numerical breakdown of the alleged cost adjustment and clarify whether ancillary costs have been shifted into the net rent.

scope: a tenant challenging a rent increase, including nullity for defect of form

requests.why: The current official rent-increase notice and any accompanying explanation are needed to verify its contents, stated basis, and formal validity.
Proof of the notice’s delivery date is needed to calculate and preserve the 30-day challenge deadline.
Final project completion, actual value-adding costs, and any subsidies must be established because the works remain incomplete and the notice relies on a provisional estimate.
A conciliation request is needed to preserve the challenge deadline for the current rent-increase notice.
These documents are needed to verify the prescribed-form notice, its stated grounds and effective date, and the date of receipt for the 30-day challenge deadline.
They are needed to establish whether the works are complete and to obtain final cost, invoice, and subsidy information supporting the renovation-related increase.
A conciliation request is needed to preserve a timely challenge to the current rent-increase notice if it has not already been submitted.
